sentences.zh: 自昔帝王受命，驅策羣力，以有天下。

translations.literal: From antiquity, when emperors received the Mandate of Heaven, they drove and marshaled the multitude of forces to possess the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, whenever an emperor accepted Heaven's mandate, he mobilized the collective strength of his followers to win the empire.

sentences.zh: 迨區宇既甯，疇庸論功，列爵崇報，壹時攀鱗附翼之士，奮起兜牟之中，剖符析珪，爰及苗裔，德意厚矣。

translations.literal: When the realm was already at peace, they assessed merit and discussed achievements, ranked nobilities and honored with reward; for a moment those who climbed the dragon's scales and attached to its wings, rising from helmet and armor, received split tally and carved jade tally, reaching even to descendants—the gracious intent was profound.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empire was secure, rulers weighed merit and rewarded service, ennobling their supporters. Men who had seized their chance beside the throne, risen from the ranks, and received fiefs and insignia—even their descendants—were treated with extraordinary generosity.

translations.literal: From the Tang and Song onward, it differed somewhat from the former system.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tang and Song dynasties onward, the practice diverged somewhat from earlier custom.

sentences.zh: 房、喬遠勢，首讓世封，是以英、衛子孫，齒于甿隸。

translations.literal: Fang and Qiao, with far-reaching influence, were first to yield hereditary enfeoffment; thus the descendants of Ying and Wei ranked equal with commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Qiao Songzhou, wielding great influence, were the first to decline perpetual enfeoffments—so the lines of Ying and Wei sank to the level of commoners.

sentences.zh: 而宋代勳階祇崇虛號，祖孫父子各擬名邦，初無世及之文，非復承家之舊。

translations.literal: In the Song dynasty, merit ranks honored only empty titles; grandfathers, fathers, and sons each bore nominal fief names, at first without the language of hereditary succession, no longer the old practice of inheriting the household.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, ennoblement chiefly bestowed hollow titles: forebears and sons alike received nominal territorial designations, but without formal hereditary succession—nothing like the old custom of passing a house from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 至明祖開基，乃曠然復古。

translations.literal: When the founding ancestor of Ming opened the foundation, he broadly restored antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming founder established his dynasty, he boldly revived ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 凡熊罴之宿將，帷幄之謀臣，生著號而殁襲封，茅土之頒，殆逾百數。

translations.literal: All veteran generals of bear-and-leopard valor and stratagem ministers within the curtains—living they bore titles and dead their enfeoffments were inherited—the granting of feudal estates nearly exceeded a hundred in number.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran commanders and chief advisors alike received titles in life and hereditary fiefs after death; patent estates were granted to more than a hundred families.

sentences.zh: 馴及季年，黨獄蔓延，剗削芟殊，存者不及三四。

translations.literal: Reaching the final years, factional prison cases spread; cutting away and uprooting was extreme, and those remaining did not reach three or four tenths.
translations.idiomatic: By the dynasty's late years, factional prosecutions swept the court. Massive purges left scarcely thirty or forty percent of these houses standing.

sentences.zh: 然觀鐵榜所列，訓誡之辭，則河山之誓，白馬之盟，初意固不其然。

translations.literal: Yet observing what the iron tablet listed, the language of instruction and admonition—then the oath upon the rivers and mountains and the white-horse covenant, their original intent was certainly not thus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet reading the inscriptions on the iron merit tablet—the warnings inscribed there—shows that the sworn oaths of old were never meant to end this way.

sentences.zh: 高危滿溢，亦其自取焉耳。

translations.literal: Danger high and brimming over—they took it upon themselves, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Their lofty peril and overflowing fortune were largely of their own making.

sentences.zh: 乃若文皇差「靖難」之勞，英宗懋「奪門」之賞，迹參佐命，籍次元功，以視開國諸臣，亦喝可同年而語乎！

translations.literal: As for Emperor Wen's lowering of merit for "Pacifying Difficulties," and Emperor Yingzong's lavish reward for "Securing the Gate," their tracks participated in assisting the mandate, registered under secondary merit—compared with the founding ministers, how can they be spoken of in the same year?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chenghua discounted the labors of the "Pacifying Difficulties" faction and Emperor Yingzong heaped honors on the "Recovering the Throne" party—men who had aided enthronement but ranked as secondary founders—how can they be named in the same breath as the dynastic founders?

sentences.zh: 世宗中葉，開冊府之舊藏，修繼絕之墜典，于是鄂、曹、衛、信之裔，復列徹侯，延其世緒，天下翕然歸厚。

translations.literal: In the mid-reign of Emperor Shizong, he opened the old repositories of the archive bureau and repaired the fallen statutes of continuing severed lines; thereby the descendants of E, Cao, Wei, and Xin again were listed as full marquises, extending their lineages—and all under Heaven united in returning to generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through Emperor Jiajing's reign, the court reopened the old archives and revived the ritual of restoring extinct noble lines. Descendants of the E, Cao, Wei, and Xin houses were reinstated as full marquises, their genealogies continued, and the realm responded with widespread approval.

sentences.zh: 雖宋、颍、韓、泣終于剿絕，而自余推誠宣力、名載丹書者，奕葉貂蟬，保守祿位，典宿衛，領京營，鎮陪京，督漕運，寄隆方嶽，階晉公孤，家分典瑞之榮，朝無酎金之罰，較諸西京世胄，殆將過之。

translations.literal: Although Song, Ying, Han, and Mu ended in extirpation, yet among the rest who pushed sincerity and declared effort, their names recorded on cinnabar books—for generations wolf-fur caps and cicada insignia, preserving salary and position, presiding over palace guard, leading capital camps, garrisoning the companion capital, supervising grain transport, entrusted with eminent frontier posts, ranks advancing to duke and regent, families sharing the glory of ritual regalia, the court without the wine-tax fine—compared with Western Han hereditary houses, they would nearly surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Song, Ying, Han, and Mu lines were eventually wiped out, the other men whose loyalty was recorded in the ledgers of merit passed down ermine ranks and court insignia through generation after generation. They kept their stipends, commanded the palace guard and capital armies, garrisoned the secondary capital, oversaw grain transport, and held the empire's weightiest provincial posts, rising to the highest ranks. Their clans enjoyed ceremonial honors unknown to the Han practice of stripping titles for insufficient tribute. In many respects they outdid the hereditary nobility of the Western Han.

sentences.zh: 今考其襲替歲月見于實錄者，作功臣表，以與紀傳相表裏。

translations.literal: Now examining the years of inheritance and replacement appearing in the veritable records, I compose the table of meritorious ministers to serve as outer and inner complement to the annals and biographies.
translations.idiomatic: I now compile a table of meritorious ministers from the succession dates recorded in the Veritable Records, to accompany the annals and biographies.

sentences.zh: 或抵牾散轶，時世無可考稽，則略而不書，固史氏阙文之義云爾。

translations.literal: Where there is contradiction, scattering, or omission, and the age affords no verification, then I omit writing—this is the meaning of the historian's omitted text.
translations.idiomatic: Where records conflict, are incomplete, or cannot be verified, I leave the entry blank, in keeping with the historian's right to omit what cannot be known.

cells.content: 魏國公 徐達 吳元年九月辛丑以平吳功，封信國公。洪武三年十一月丙申大封功臣，進封奉天開國推誠宣力武臣魏國公，祿五千石，世襲。十八年二月己未卒。追封中山王，諡武寧。達初封公，位次第二。李善長得罪，進位第一。

translations.literal: Duke of Wei Xu Da: On the xinchou day of the ninth month of the Wu era year, for merit in pacifying Wu, enfeoffed as Duke of Xin. On the bingshen day of the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, in the great enfeoffment of meritorious ministers, advanced to Duke of Wei, "Loyal and Sincere in Opening the State, Pushing Sincerity and Declaring Force, Martial Minister," stipend five thousand piculs, hereditary. On the jiwei day of the second month of year 18 he died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan, posthumous name Wuning. When Da was first enfeoffed as duke, his rank was second. When Li Shanzhang was condemned, he advanced to first.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Wei, Xu Da: In the ninth month of the Wu era, he was made Duke of Xin for conquering Wu. At the great enfeoffment of Hongwu 3 he was raised to Duke of Wei with a stipend of five thousand piculs and hereditary succession. He died in the second month of Hongwu 18 and was posthumously created Prince of Zhongshan with the temple name Wuning. Xu Da had originally ranked second among the ennobled; after Li Shanzhang's fall he moved to first place.

translations.literal: Huizu: On the bingyin day of the tenth month of Hongwu year 21 he inherited, heading the Central Military Commission. At the beginning of Jianwen, added Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent. When Emperor Wen acceded, his nobility was stripped. He died in the fifth year of Yongle.

translations.literal: Qin: On the xinsi day of the seventh month of Yongle year 5 he inherited. On the renchen day of the first month of year 19 his nobility was stripped. On the yisi day of the tenth month of year 22 it was restored. On the gengzi day of the eleventh month of that year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qin inherited in the seventh month of Yongle 5. In the first month of Yongle 19 his title was revoked, but in the tenth month of Yongle 22 it was restored. He died that same winter.

Chengzong: On the wuzi day of the seventh month of Zhengtong year 13 he inherited, heading the Forward Commission. On the gengyin day of the twelfth month of Tianshun year 7 he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong succeeded in the third month of Hongxi 1 and died in Zhengtong 13. Chengzong inherited that summer, commanded the Forward Commission, and died in the twelfth month of Tianshun 7.

translations.literal: Fu: In Chenghua 1 he inherited. In the ninth year of Hongzhi he garrisoned Nanjing. In the seventh month of the fifth year of Zhengde he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent. On the bingxu day of the seventh month of year 12 he died. Posthumous name Zhuangjing.

translations.literal: Pengju: On the guihai day of the eleventh month of Zhengde year 13 he inherited, garrisoning Nanjing and concurrently serving as secretary of the Central Commission. In the fourth year of Jiajing he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and headed the Central Commission. On the renxu day of the fourth month of year 17 he garrisoned Nanjing. On the xinchou day of the second month of Longqing year 5 he died.
translations.idiomatic: Pengju inherited in the eleventh month of Zhengde 13, defending Nanjing while serving on the Central Military Commission. In Jiajing 4 he became Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and headed that commission. He again defended Nanjing in the fourth month of Jiajing 17 and died in the second month of Longqing 5.

translations.literal: Hongji: On the jihai day of the seventh month of Wanli year 23 he inherited, secretary of the Nanjing military commissions. In year 35 he jointly garrisoned Nanjing and headed the Rear Commission. In the fourth month of year 37 he supervised operations on the Yangtze. In the first year of Tianqi, citing illness he resigned his post and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen he again garrisoned Nanjing and was made Grand Tutor. On death, posthumous name Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji inherited in the seventh month of Wanli 23 and served on the Nanjing military commissions. In Wanli 35 he jointly defended Nanjing and headed the Rear Commission; in Wanli 37 he took charge of the Yangtze fleet. Illness forced his resignation in Tianqi 1, though he received the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. He returned to defend Nanjing in Chongzhen 14 as Grand Tutor and was posthumously named Zhuangwu.

translations.literal: Duke of Han Li Shanzhang: On the xinchou day of the ninth month of the Wu era year enfeoffed as Duke of Xuan. On the bingshen day of the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, in the great enfeoffment of meritorious ministers, first rank, enfeoffed as Duke of Han, "Assisting Transport in Opening the State, Pushing Sincerity, Upholding Culture, Civil Minister," stipend four thousand piculs, hereditary. On the yimao day of the fifth month of year 23 he was condemned as a member of Hu Weiyong's faction and executed; the nobility was abolished. On the guisi day of the seventh month of the second year of Chongzhen, descendant Shixuan presented the founding ancestor's handwritten edict, containing the words "two hundred and sixty springs, coming to present at the appointed season." Grand Secretary Han Kuang impeached him for fraud; he was imprisoned and sentenced to death, but afterward was released.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Han, Li Shanzhang: Made Duke of Xuan in the ninth month of the Wu era and ranked first at the great enfeoffment of Hongwu 3 as Duke of Han with four thousand piculs and hereditary succession. Executed for ties to Hu Weiyong's faction in the fifth month of Hongwu 23, his line was extinguished. In the seventh month of Chongzhen 2, a descendant named Shixuan presented an alleged handwritten edict of the founder containing a prophecy of return after "two hundred and sixty springs." Grand Secretary Han Kuang denounced the document as a forgery; Shixuan was condemned to death but later released.

translations.literal: Wenming: On the gengzi day of the second month of the first year of Chongzhen he inherited. In the third month of the seventeenth year, when the city fell, he died at the hands of bandits.

translations.literal: Duke of Xin Tang He: In the great enfeoffment of meritorious ministers of Hongwu year 3, seventh rank, enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongshan, "Assisting Transport in Opening the State, Pushing Sincerity, Declaring Force, Martial Minister," stipend one thousand five hundred piculs. On the yimao day of the eighth month of year 7, stipend increased by one thousand piculs. On the jimao day of the first month of year 11 he was advanced to Duke of Xin, stipend three thousand piculs, hereditary. On the wuchen day of the eighth month of year 28 he died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dong'ou, posthumous name Xiangwu.

translations.literal: Shilong: On the jihai day of the tenth month of Jiajing year 39 he inherited. He died in the fourteenth year of Wanli. Posthumous name Ximin.

translations.literal: Marquis of Yan'an Tang Shengzong: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, eighth rank, merit stipend as before. On the yimao day of the eighth month of year 7, stipend increased by one thousand piculs; for an offense his nobility was stripped. After a long time the nobility was restored. In year 23 he was condemned as a member of Hu's faction and executed; the nobility was abolished.

Executed for ties to Hu Weiyong's faction in Hongwu 23, his line ended.

translations.literal: Marquis of Changxing Geng Bingwen: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, thirteenth rank, merit stipend as before. translations.literal: Marquis of Xingyang Zheng Yuchun: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, seventeenth rank; merit stipend and added stipend were both the same as Wang Zhi. In year 23 he was condemned as a member of Hu's faction and executed; the line was abolished.

translations.literal: Marquis of Pingliang Fei Ju: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, eighteenth rank, merit title as before, stipend one thousand five hundred piculs. In the eighth month of year 7 stipend increased by one thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Gao: On the xinyou day of the fifth month of Hongwu year 17 he inherited. In year 28, for an offense he was banished to Guangxi; afterward he was summoned back. During Jianwen, because of being slandered he was banished again. When Emperor Wen acceded, he was summoned to defend Datong. In the tenth month of the twelfth year of Yongle he was dismissed for a crime; on death the line was abolished.

translations.literal: Marquis of Guangde Hua Gao: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, twenty-fourth rank, merit title as before, stipend six hundred piculs. On the yiwei day of the fourth month of year 4 he died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Chao, posthumous name Wuzhuang. Without a son, the nobility was abolished.

cells.content: 營陽侯 楊璟 洪武三年十一月封，第二十五，勳號同前，祿一千五百石。七年加祿千石。十五年八月乙巳卒。追封芮國公，諡武信。

translations.literal: Marquis of Yingyang Yang Jing: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, twenty-fifth rank, merit title as before, stipend one thousand five hundred piculs. In year 7 stipend increased by one thousand piculs. On the yisi day of the eighth month of year 15 he died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Rui, posthumous name Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Yingyang, Yang Jing: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu 3, ranking twenty-fifth with fifteen hundred piculs. His stipend was raised in Hongwu 7. He died in the eighth month of Hongwu 15 and was posthumously created Duke of Rui with the temple name Wuxin.

cells.content: 通 洪武十七年十一月丁酉襲。二十年降指揮使，已，追坐璟胡黨，除。

translations.literal: Tong: On the dingyou day of the eleventh month of Hongwu year 17 he inherited. In year 20 he was demoted to commandant; afterward he was posthumously charged as a member of Jing's Hu faction and the line was abolished.

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Kang Maocai: On the jiwei day of the eighth month of Hongwu year 3 he died in the army. Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, "Meritorious Minister Who Pushes Loyalty, Assists Transport, Declares Force, and Cherishes the Distance," posthumous name Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Qi, Kang Maocai: Died on campaign in the eighth month of Hongwu 3 and was posthumously created Duke of Qi with the temple name Wukang.

translations.literal: Duo: In the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3 enfeoffed as Marquis of Qichun, twenty-sixth rank; merit stipend and added stipend the same as Yang Jing. On the bingzi day of the seventh month of year 15 he died and was granted Duke of Qi, posthumous name Zhongmin. His son Yuan was young and received favorable treatment; afterward he received reprimand and died, and the nobility was abolished.

translations.literal: Marquis of Yongjia Zhu Liangzu: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, twenty-seventh rank; merit stipend and added stipend the same as Yang Jing. On the gengyin day of the ninth month of year 13 he was condemned for a crime and executed; the nobility was abolished.

translations.literal: Duke of Ying Fu Youde: In the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3 enfeoffed as Marquis of Yingchuan, twenty-eighth rank, merit stipend as before. On the xinmao day of the fourth month of year 17 he was advanced to Duke of Ying, stipend three thousand piculs, hereditary. On the yichou day of the eleventh month of year 27 he was granted death; the nobility was abolished.

translations.literal: Marquis of Linchuan Hu Mei: In the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3 enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuzhang, twenty-ninth rank; merit stipend and added stipend the same as Yang Jing. On the yichou day of the fourth month of year 13 his title was changed to Linchuan. In year 17, guilty of an offense, he was granted death; the nobility was abolished.

translations.literal: Marquis of Dongping Han Zheng: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, thirtieth rank; merit stipend and added stipend as before. On the guihai day of the second month of year 11 he died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yun.

cells.content: 勳 洪武十九年十一月甲子襲。二十六年坐藍黨死，爵除。

translations.literal: Marquis of Yichun Huang Bin: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, thirty-first rank; merit stipend and added stipend the same as Wang Zhi. In year 23 he was condemned as a member of Hu's faction and executed; the nobility was abolished.

translations.literal: Marquis of Xuanning Cao Liangchen: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, thirty-second rank, merit stipend the same as Wang Zhi. translations.literal: Tai: On the yisi day of the fifth month of Hongwu year 6 he inherited. In the eighth month of year 7 stipend increased to two thousand five hundred piculs. In year 26 he was condemned as a member of Lan Yu's faction and executed; the nobility was abolished.

translations.literal: Marquis of Runan Mei Sizu: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, thirty-third rank; merit stipend and added stipend the same as Wang Zhi. translations.literal: Earl of Zhongqin Wang Guangyang: In the eleventh month of Hongwu year 3, as a civil minister he was enfeoffed, stipend three hundred sixty piculs. In the eighth month of year 7 stipend increased to one thousand nine hundred piculs. In year 12 he died after demotion.

In the twelfth month of the eighth year of Zhengde he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, posthumous name Wencheng.

translations.literal: Marquis of Yongcheng Xue Xian: On the wuchen day of the twelfth month of Hongwu year 3 he was enfeoffed. For a crime he was resettled in Hainan. Afterward he was summoned back and granted a stipend of one thousand five hundred piculs. On the guisi day of the ninth month of year 20 he died in the army. Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yong, posthumous name Huanxiang. Without a son. Later charged as a member of Hu's faction; because he was dead it was not pursued, but the line was abolished.

Having no heir, the line was later implicated in Hu Weiyong's faction and ended.

cells.content: 春 洪武二十五年十月乙亥襲，鎮雲南。三十一年卒。諡惠襄。 昂 景泰中贈定邊伯。 黔國公 晟 洪武三十一年襲侯。永樂六年七月以征安南功，進封公，祿三千石，世襲，世鎮雲南。仁宗即位，加太傅，支二俸。正統四年三月丁卯卒。追封定遠王，諡忠敬。

translations.literal: Chun: On the yihai day of the tenth month of Hongwu year 25 he inherited and garrisoned Yunnan. He died in the thirty-first year. Posthumous name Huixiang. Ang: During Jingtai he was granted Marquis of Dingbian. Duke of Qian Sheng: In the thirty-first year of Hongwu he inherited the marquisate. When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was made Grand Tutor and drew two salaries. On the dingmao day of the third month of the fourth year of Zhengtong he died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dingyuan, posthumous name Zhongjing.

translations.literal: Tianbo: On the jiachen day of the twelfth month of the first year of Chongzhen he inherited. On the jiayin day of the eighth month of the seventh year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. After the fall of Ming, he followed the Prince of Gui into Burma and died in the calamity.

translations.literal: Marquis of Anqing Qiu Cheng: On the jiawu day of the eleventh month of Hongwu year 12 he was enfeoffed, stipend two thousand piculs, hereditary commandant. On the renwu day of the fourth month of year 17 he was granted hereditary marquisate and stipend increased by five hundred piculs. On the xinsi day of the seventh month of year 21 he died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Wan, posthumous name Zhuangxiang.

translations.literal: Duke of Liang Lan Yu: On the jiawu day of the eleventh month of Hongwu year 12 he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchang, stipend and inheritance as before. On the renwu day of the fourth month of year 17 he was granted hereditary marquisate and stipend increased by five hundred piculs. On the renxu day of the twelfth month of year 21 he was advanced to duke and stipend increased by five hundred piculs. On the yiyou day of the second month of year 26 he plotted rebellion and was executed.

cells.content: 永平侯 謝成 洪武十二年十一月封，祿襲同仇成。二十六年坐累卒。

translations.literal: Marquis of Fengxiang Zhang Long: Enfeoffed in the twelfth month of Hongwu year 12, stipend and inheritance as before. Later granted hereditary succession and stipend increased by five hundred piculs. He died in the thirtieth year.

translations.literal: Jie: Inherited during Jianwen. Abolished at the beginning of Yongle.

translations.literal: Marquis of Anlu Wu Fu: Enfeoffed in the twelfth month of Hongwu year 12, stipend and inheritance as before. On the jihai day of the tenth month of year 16 he died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Qian, posthumous name Wuyi, stipend increased by five hundred piculs, hereditary.

translations.literal: Marquis of Xuande Jin Chaoxing: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 12, stipend and inheritance as before. On the bingzi day of the seventh month of year 15 he died. The next year he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yi, posthumous name Wuyi. In year 17 hereditary succession was granted and stipend increased by five hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Marquis of Xiongwu Zhou Wu: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 12, stipend and inheritance as before. On the gengwu day of the third month of year 23 he died. translations.literal: Marquis of Dingyuan Wang Bi: Enfeoffed in the eleventh month of Hongwu year 12, stipend and inheritance as before. In the fourth month of year 17 stipend increased to two thousand five hundred piculs. On the yihai day of the twelfth month of year 27 he died.

On the bingwu day of the seventh month of the twelfth year he died. Because his sons disputed the succession, the inheritance was suspended.

cells.content: 良 弘治十五年四月癸丑襲。十一月坐効勇營管操。正德二年六月戊子卒。

translations.literal: Liang: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi he inherited. In the eleventh month he was put in charge of drilling the Xiaoyong Camp. On the wuzi day of the sixth month of the second year of Zhengde he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liang inherited in the fourth month of Hongzhi 15, took charge of drilling the Xiaoyong Camp in the eleventh month, and died in the sixth month of Zhengde 2.

cells.content: 勛 正德三年三月丙寅襲，鎮兩廣，屢兼軍府。四年八月，神機營管操。嘉靖十八年進封翊國公，加太師，前後益祿四百石。二十年九月有罪下獄，明年卒於獄。

translations.literal: Xun: On the bingyin day of the third month of the third year of Zhengde he inherited, garrisoning the Two Guangs and repeatedly holding military commissions. In the eighth month of the fourth year he drilled the Divine Engine Camp. In the eighteenth year of Jiajing he was advanced to Duke of Yiguo, made Grand Preceptor, and his stipend was increased by four hundred piculs before and after. In the ninth month of the twentieth year he was imprisoned for a crime; the next year he died in prison.

translations.literal: Shouqian: On the renchen day of the third month of the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing he inherited, repeatedly heading military commissions. On the dingyou day of the fourth month of the thirty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqian inherited in the third month of Jiajing 29, repeatedly commanded military offices, and died in the fourth month of Jiajing 39.

translations.literal: Dacheng: On the gengxu day of the third month of the forty-fourth year of Jiajing he inherited. In the fifth month of the forty-fifth year he drilled the Red-Helmet Guards. In the fourth year of Wanli he headed the Nanjing Right Commission. On the guihai day of the sixth month of the forty-fourth year he died.

translations.literal: Yingqi: On the renzi day of the second month of the forty-fifth year of Wanli he inherited and soon died. Yinglin: On the jiaxu day of the eleventh month of the forty-fifth year of Wanli he inherited. He died in the first year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqi inherited in the second month of Wanli 45 and died soon after. Yinglin inherited that winter and died in Chongzhen 1.

cells.content: 培民 崇禎初襲。三年九月甲辰加太子太保。十七年三月，城陷死。

translations.literal: Peimin: Inherited at the beginning of Chongzhen. On the jiachen day of the ninth month of the third year he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. In the third month of the seventeenth year, when the city fell, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Peimin inherited at the start of Chongzhen, became Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent in the ninth month of Chongzhen 3, and was killed when the capital fell in the third month of Chongzhen 17.

cells.content: 鶴慶侯 張翼 洪武十七年四月封，祿襲同前。二十六年坐藍黨誅。

translations.literal: Marquis of Heqing Zhang Yi: Enfeoffed in the fourth month of Hongwu year 17, stipend and inheritance as before. In year 26 he was condemned as a member of Lan Yu's faction and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Heqing, Zhang Yi: Enfeoffed in the fourth month of Hongwu 17. Executed for ties to Lan Yu's faction in Hongwu 26.

cells.content: 航海侯 張赫 洪武二十年十月戊申封，祿二千石，世襲。二十三年八月甲子卒。追封恩國公，諡莊簡。子停襲。

translations.literal: Marquis of Hanghai Zhang He: On the wushen day of the tenth month of Hongwu year 20 he was enfeoffed, stipend two thousand piculs, hereditary. On the jiazi day of the eighth month of year 23 he died. Posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of En, posthumous name Zhuangjian. His son Ting inherited.

cells.content: 舳艫侯 朱壽 洪武二十年十月封，祿襲同前。二十六年坐藍黨誅，除。

translations.literal: Marquis of Zhulu Zhu Shou: Enfeoffed in the tenth month of Hongwu year 20, stipend and inheritance as before. In year 26 he was condemned as a member of Lan Yu's faction and executed; the line was abolished.

translations.literal: Marquis of Haixi Nahachu: In the ninth month of the twentieth year of Wu he was enfeoffed as a Yuan defector general. On the xinchou day of the seventh month of the twenty-first year he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Haixi, Nahachu: Enfeoffed in the ninth month of the Wu era's twentieth year as a surrendered Yuan general. He died on campaign in the seventh month of the twenty-first year.

cells.content: 察罕 洪武二十一年八月襲，改封瀋陽侯。二十六年四月壬午坐藍黨誅，除。

translations.literal: Chahan: In the eighth month of Hongwu year 21 he inherited; his title was changed to Marquis of Shenyang. On the renwu day of the fourth month of year 26 he was condemned as a member of Lan Yu's faction and executed; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan inherited in the eighth month of Hongwu 21 and was re-titled Marquis of Shenyang. Executed for ties to Lan Yu's faction in the fourth month of Hongwu 26; his line ended.

translations.literal: Earl of Dongguan He Zhen: Enfeoffed in the seventh month of Hongwu year 20, stipend one thousand five hundred piculs, hereditary. On the jimao day of the third month of year 21 he died.
translations.idiomatic: Earl of Dongguan, He Zhen: Enfeoffed in the seventh month of Hongwu 20 with fifteen hundred piculs and hereditary rank. He died in the third month of Hongwu 21.

translations.literal: Rong: On the yisi day of the fourth month of Hongwu year 21 he inherited. In year 26 he was condemned as a member of Lan Yu's faction and executed; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 全寧侯 孫恪 興祖子。洪武二十一年八月戊辰封，祿二千石，世襲。坐藍黨死，除。

translations.literal: Marquis of Quanning Sun Ke, son of Sun Xingzu: On the wuchen day of the eighth month of Hongwu year 21 he was enfeoffed, stipend two thousand piculs, hereditary. He was condemned as a member of Lan Yu's faction and executed; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Quanning, Sun Ke, son of Sun Xingzu: Enfeoffed in the eighth month of Hongwu 21 with two thousand piculs and hereditary rank. Executed for ties to Lan Yu's faction; his line ended.

cells.content: 樂浪公 濮英 洪武二十年閏六月庚申戰歿金山。追封金山侯，諡忠襄。二十一年七月進封公。

translations.literal: Duke of Lelang Pu Ying: On the gengshen day of the intercalary sixth month of Hongwu year 20 he was killed in battle at Jinshan. Posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Jinshan, posthumous name Zhongxiang. In the seventh month of year 21 he was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Lelang, Pu Ying: Killed in battle at Jinshan in the intercalary sixth month of Hongwu 20. Posthumously made Marquis of Jinshan with the temple name Zhongxiang, then advanced to duke in the seventh month of Hongwu 21.

cells.content: 璵 洪武二十一年九月丙戌封西涼侯，祿二千五百石，世襲。二十六年追坐英藍黨，謫戍，除。

translations.literal: Yu: On the bingxu day of the ninth month of Hongwu year 21 he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiliang, stipend two thousand five hundred piculs, hereditary. In year 26 he was posthumously charged as a member of Ying's and Lan's factions, banished to garrison duty, and the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiliang in the ninth month of Hongwu 21 with twenty-five hundred piculs and hereditary rank. In Hongwu 26 he was posthumously implicated in Pu Ying's and Lan Yu's factions, exiled, and the line ended.

translations.literal: Earl of Huixian Sang Jing, son of Shi Jie: On the renyin day of the ninth month of Hongwu year 23 he was enfeoffed, stipend one thousand seven hundred piculs, hereditary. Afterward he was condemned as a member of Lan Yu's faction and executed; the line was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Earl of Huixian, Sang Jing, son of Shi Jie: Enfeoffed in the ninth month of Hongwu 23 with seventeen hundred piculs and hereditary rank. Later executed for ties to Lan Yu's faction; his line ended.

translations.literal: Marquis of Yongding Zhang Quan: On the jiashen day of the tenth month of Hongwu year 23 he was enfeoffed, stipend one thousand five hundred piculs, hereditary commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Yongding, Zhang Quan: Enfeoffed in the tenth month of Hongwu 23 with fifteen hundred piculs and hereditary commandant rank.

cells.content: 越巂侯 俞淵 洪武二十五年六月戊午封，祿二千五百石，世襲。明年五月戊辰削爵，放還里。建文初，召還，戰歿白溝河。永樂初除。

translations.literal: Marquis of Yuexi Yu Yuan: On the wuwu day of the sixth month of Hongwu year 25 he was enfeoffed, stipend two thousand five hundred piculs, hereditary. On the wuchen day of the fifth month of the next year his nobility was stripped and he was sent home. At the beginning of Jianwen he was recalled, and died in battle at the Baigou River. Abolished at the beginning of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 以上皆身受封，或不及封而子孫封者。

translations.literal: The above all personally received enfeoffment, or though they did not reach enfeoffment themselves, their descendants were enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Those listed above were enfeoffed in person, or—though they themselves were not enfeoffed—their descendants received titles.

sentences.zh: 其追贈封爵無世系可譜，別以五等爲次，具列於左。

translations.literal: Those posthumously granted enfeoffment with no genealogy that can be traced are separately arranged by the five ranks, fully listed at left.
